title: QCon AI New York 2026: Registration Opens for December 15-16 Production-AI Conference
gist: A short registration announcement for QCon AI New York (December 15-16, The Westin Jersey City Newport) whose only real signal is the agenda: the practitioner program committee has organised the whole event around six production-AI problem areas — agent runtime design, context engineering, evals and observability, MCP and tool access, zero-trust security for tool-using agents, and inference cost and latency. The event is explicitly aimed at teams already running AI in production rather than teams deciding whether to adopt.

themes.theme: The six production-AI problems a practitioner committee picked

insights.claim: The QCon AI New York 2026 program committee organised the entire two-day agenda around six production-AI areas: agent runtime design (state ownership, recovery, approval boundaries for long-running agents), context engineering, evals and observability, MCP and tool access, zero-trust security for tool-using agents, and inference cost and latency.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: This is a practitioner-curated map of where enterprise AI money and engineering effort is actually going in late 2026 — a category list for sizing tooling vendors in each slot.
insights.quote: Agent runtime design, covering state ownership, recovery, and approval boundaries for long-running agents
insights.locator: 'The program committee has organized the program around six areas'

insights.claim: The stated rationale for those six areas is that each is a problem teams tend to hit only once an AI feature moves past a demo and has to survive real traffic in production, positioning the demo-to-production gap as the industry's current bottleneck.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Vendors solving demo-stage problems face a shrinking market; the budget is moving to runtime, evals, security and cost-control tooling.
insights.quote: Each addresses a problem teams tend to hit once an AI feature moves past a demo and has to survive real traffic in production.

themes.theme: Audience shift from AI adopters to AI operators

insights.claim: The conference explicitly targets senior engineers, architects and engineering leaders who already own AI systems running in production, rather than teams still deciding whether to adopt AI — an audience-definition shift away from evaluation-stage buyers.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: A read on where the enterprise AI buying cycle sits: the addressable audience is now operators, not evaluators.
insights.quote: who own AI systems running in production, rather than teams still deciding whether to adopt AI

insights.claim: Every proposed session is reviewed against two gates — whether the speaker has actually run the systems and models in production, and whether they will discuss what did not work alongside what did — with sessions invite-only and no sponsored talks or product pitches on the main schedule.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: A failure-disclosure requirement makes this agenda a rarer source of negative results on production AI than vendor-run events — worth reading the eventual talk list as a due-diligence input.
insights.quote: The committee reviews every proposed session against two questions: whether the speaker has run the systems and models in production, and whether they will discuss what didn't work alongside what did.

insights.claim: The program is chaired by Eder Ignatowicz, senior principal software engineer and architect at Red Hat AI, joined by Faye Zhang, staff engineer and GenAI search tech lead at Google, and Wes Reisz, technical principal consultant at Thoughtworks.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Committee composition (Red Hat, Google, Thoughtworks) signals whose view of the production-AI stack shapes the agenda enterprises will see.
insights.locator: 'The program is chaired by Eder Ignatowicz'

insights.claim: QCon AI New York is the second of only two QCon AI events on the 2026 calendar, following QCon AI Boston earlier in the year, with first sessions announced in August, a preliminary schedule in October and the complete program by early November.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: The August session announcement is the earliest date at which the concrete production-AI case studies become readable — a calendar marker, not a thesis.
insights.locator: 'QCon AI New York is the second of two QCon AI events'
